questions.q_en:
In the sentence below, identify the type of conjunction of the word “although”:

Although the organization faced severe financial difficulties during the previous year, it continued funding educational programs in rural areas.
questions.q_hi:
In the sentence below, identify the type of conjunction of the word “although”:

Although the organization faced severe financial difficulties during the previous year, it continued funding educational programs in rural areas.
questions.solution_en:
Answer: C) Subordinating Conjunction

Explanation: A subordinating conjunction joins a dependent clause to an independent clause.

Here, “although” introduces the dependent clause:

“Although the organization faced severe financial difficulties during the previous year”

This clause cannot stand alone and depends on the main clause for complete meaning.

Therefore, “although” is a subordinating conjunction.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

Should the lead investigator _________ to conclude that the evidence was tampered with, the department _________ likely be able to prosecute the suspect.
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

Should the lead investigator _________ to conclude that the evidence was tampered with, the department _________ likely be able to prosecute the suspect.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is Option (b): need / will.

Blank 1: "Should the lead investigator _________ to conclude..."

Concept: Conditional Inversion: The sentence begins with "Should" at the start of the clause, which is a formal way of saying "If".

Grammar Rule: When a sentence starts with "Should" (meaning "If"), it functions as the auxiliary verb for that clause. Any subsequent verb must be in its base form (V1) because it is governed by "Should".

Even though "investigator" is a third-person singular subject, the "s" is dropped because of the formal inversion. You would say "Should he go," not "Should he goes".

Blank 2: "...the department _________ likely be able to prosecute..."

Concept: Redundancy of Possibility: In English grammar, you cannot pair two words of the same "uncertainty" in the same clause.

"May" + "likely": This is redundant (Superfluous Expression) because both express possibility.

"Can" + "able to": This is also redundant because both express ability.

Key Takeaways -

  1. The Inversion Trigger: When you see "Should" at the start of a statement, look for a base form verb (V1) without an 's'.

  2. The Redundancy Filter: When you see "likely," "possibly," or "able to," filter out modals like May, Might, or Can to avoid the "Superfluous Expression".

options_en: Both the team captains, who had spent weeks preparing their presentations
have presented their strategies to the audience with confidence, illustrating his innovative ideas

questions.q_en:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

"Don't enter without permission!"
questions.q_hi:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

"Don't enter without permission!"
options_en: You asked me not to enter without permission.
You forbade me not to enter without permission.
You told me to not enter without permission.
You forbade me to enter without permission.
options_hi: You asked me not to enter without permission.
You forbade me not to enter without permission.
You told me to not enter without permission.
You forbade me to enter without permission.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is Option D: You forbade me to enter without permission.

Key Points

  • Identification of Sentence Type: The sentence is an imperative sentence containing a negative command ("Don't").

  • Implied Speaker and Receiver: Similar to your demo image, the speaker and receiver are not explicitly named in the direct speech. By analyzing the options, we identify a "You" (speaker) and "Me" (receiver) relationship.

  • The "Forbid" Rule: The reporting verb forbade (past tense of forbid) inherently means "ordered/commanded NOT to."

    • Because the negative meaning is built into the verb itself, the reported clause becomes affirmative.

    • Correct: forbade + object + to + verb.

    • Incorrect: forbade + object + not to + verb (this is a double negative and would technically mean you were ordered to enter).

  • Eliminating Incorrect Options:

    • Option A is grammatically possible but changes the tone from a command to a request ("asked").

    • Option B is the classic trap; it uses "forbade" and "not" together, which is grammatically redundant.

    • Option C uses "to not enter," which is a split infinitive and less preferred compared to "not to enter" or the "forbade" construction.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The coach insisted that the athletes must
practice their specialized drills everyday if
they intended to break the standing world record.
options_hi: The coach insisted that the athletes must
practice their specialized drills everyday if
they intended to break the standing world record.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “everyday” with “every day”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Everyday vs. Every day

  • Everyday (Adjective): It is a single word used to describe something that is ordinary, common, or used daily. It must always be followed by a noun (e.g., everyday chores, everyday clothes).

  • Every day (Adverbial Phrase): It consists of the adjective "every" and the noun "day." It functions as an adverb of frequency, telling us how often an action happens. It usually modifies a verb and answers the question "How often?

💢 Application to the Given Question

...practice their specialized drills everyday if...

In this sentence, the phrase is intended to modify the verb "practice." It describes the frequency of the action (how often they must practice). Therefore, the two-word adverbial phrase "every day" is required. Using the single-word adjective "everyday" here is ungrammatical because there is no noun following it for it to modify.

Corrected Sentence

The coach insisted that the athletes must practice their specialized drills every day if they intended to break the standing world record.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 : You need to complete your assignments every day to maintain your grades. ✅ Example 2 : These shoes are great for everyday wear because they are so comfortable. ✅

Incorrect Usage

Wrong example 1 : I go to the gym everyday to stay fit. (Should be: every day) ❌ Wrong example 2 : Losing your keys is an every day problem for the forgetful. (Should be: everyday) ❌

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  • The "Noun Test": If you can place a noun immediately after the word, use "everyday" (e.g., everyday struggle).

  • The "Each Day" Substitution: If you can replace the term with "each day" and the sentence still makes sense, use the two-word "every day."

  • Position Tip: "Every day" (two words) often appears at the beginning or the end of a clause, whereas "everyday" (one word) is almost always found right before a noun.

Techniques such as gene editing and synthetic biology offer unprecedented control over biological processes; however, critics caution that rapid innovation can [----1---] ethical scrutiny if commercial incentives dominate decision-making. Additionally, unequal access to biotechnological advances risks [---2---] existing global disparities in healthcare and food security. Public apprehension is further fueled when scientific communication remains [---3---], failing to clearly explain risks, benefits, and limitations. Experts therefore stress that responsible progress in biotechnology requires a [---4---] governance framework that aligns innovation with societal values.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [2] :

Public apprehension is further fueled when scientific communication remains [---3---], failing to clearly explain risks, benefits, and limitations. Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [2] :
options_en: mitigate
entrench
redistribute
neutralize
options_hi: mitigate

redistribute
neutralize
questions.solution_en:
Entrench means to make something more firmly established and difficult to change. The passage suggests that unequal access can deepen existing inequalities, making entrench the most accurate verb.
WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
• Mitigate means reduce severity, the opposite effect.
• Redistribute implies correcting imbalance, not worsening it.
• Neutralize suggests elimination of disparities.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Had the whistle-blower not leaked the classified
documents to the press last winter, the corporate
fraud would remained hidden from the public eye.
options_hi: Had the whistle-blower not leaked the classified
documents to the press last winter, the corporate
fraud would remained hidden from the public eye.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) - Replace “would remained” with “would have remained”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Third Conditional (Inverted Form)

The Third Conditional is used to express an unreal or hypothetical situation in the past and its probable past result. When the sentence begins with "Had" (inversion), it replaces the "If + had + V3" structure. The mandatory structure for the result clause is: Had + Subject + V3 (Past Participle) + ..., Subject + would/could/might + have + V3.

💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the condition is correctly established using "Had the whistle-blower not leaked..." (an unreal past condition). However, the result clause in Part C uses "would remained," which is grammatically incomplete. To show a past hypothetical result, "would" must be followed by "have" and the past participle (V3) "remained."

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅: Had I known about the traffic, I would have started earlier.

Example 2 ✅: Had she studied harder, she might have passed the entrance exam.

Example 3 ✅: The company could have avoided bankruptcy had it diversified its portfolio.

options_en: In order to maintain competitive pricing and international quality
standards, the board of directors decided to significantly increase
the annual production capacity of the manufacturing unit.
No Error
options_hi: In order to maintain competitive pricing and international quality
standards, the board of directors decided to significantly increase
the annual production capacity of the manufacturing unit.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “to significantly increase” with “to increase significantly”.

Rule / Concept: Split Infinitive Rule

An infinitive is the base form of a verb preceded by "to" (e.g., to eat, to increase). A Split Infinitive occurs when an adverb is placed between "to" and the "verb." it is generally considered an error to split the infinitive. The adverb should be placed after the verb or before the "to"

Application to the Given Question

"...the board of directors decided to significantly increase the annual production..."

In this sentence, the infinitive is "to increase". The adverb "significantly" has been placed between "to" and "increase," thereby splitting the infinitive. To maintain formal grammatical standards, the adverb should be moved to a position after the object or immediately following the verb.

Corrected Sentence

In order to maintain competitive pricing and international quality standards, the board of directors decided to increase significantly the annual production capacity of the manufacturing unit. (Note: "to increase the annual production capacity significantly" is also correct.)

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1: I asked him to read carefully. ✅

Example 2: She tried to explain clearly the situation. ✅

Example 3: They want to resolve quickly the dispute. ✅

Incorrect Usage

Wrong example 1: I asked him to carefully read. ❌

Wrong example 2: She tried to clearly explain the situation. ❌

Wrong example 3: They want to quickly resolve the dispute. ❌

of all non-essential travel expenses until the company
achieves its projected revenue targets for the third quarter.
No Error
options_hi: Only yesterday the regional manager announced the suspension
of all non-essential travel expenses until the company
achieves its projected revenue targets for the third quarter.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “the regional manager announced” with “did the regional manager announce”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Inversion with "Only + Time Expression"

When a sentence begins with "Only" followed by a time expression (e.g., Only yesterday, Only recently, Only then, Only last week, Only after...), the main clause must follow the Partial Inversion structure. This requires placing an auxiliary verb (do, does, did, has, have, had) before the subject.

💢 Application to the Given Question

Only yesterday the regional manager announced...

In this sentence, the restrictive time phrase "Only yesterday" is used at the beginning for emphasis. The verb "announced" is in the Simple Past tense. 📌 Rule / Concept: Simple Present Tense – Active to Passive Conversion

In the Simple Present tense, the active structure is:
Subject + V¹ / V¹+s + Object

The passive structure becomes:

Object + am/is/are + V³ (+ by + Subject)

The auxiliary verb (am/is/are) must agree with the new subject, and the main verb must be converted into its past participle (V³) form.

Hence, “are monitored” is the correct transformation.

📌 Rule / Concept: The "Until/Unless" Rule (Time & Conditional Clauses)

When a sentence refers to two actions in the future, we use the Future Tense (will + V1) in the main clause, but we never use "will" in the subordinate clause introduced by time or condition conjunctions like if, when, until, unless, before, after, or as soon as. Instead, we use the Simple Present Tense

💢 Application to the Given Question

"...protocols will remain... until every individual... undergoes..."

This sentence correctly follows the rule:

  1. Main Clause: "The security protocols will remain in effect" correctly uses the Future Tense to describe the ongoing state.

  2. Time Clause: "until every individual... undergoes..." correctly uses the Simple Present (V{s/es}) following the conjunction "until."

Even though the "undergoing" of screening will happen in the future, the grammar requires the Simple Present because "until" establishes the boundary/condition for the main action.

removed from the stove, the liquid was very hot to drink

No Error
options_hi: Even though the waiter had warned us that the soup had just been

No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “very hot to drink” with “too hot to drink”.

Rule / Concept: The "Too...To" Negative Result

he combination of Too + Adjective + To-Infinitive implies a negative result or an inability to perform an action.

  • Very simply increases the intensity of the adjective (e.g., very hot).

  • Too indicates that the intensity has reached an excessive or undesirable level that prevents the subsequent action from happening.

TOO :- (more than what is required).It is used

to qualify negative adjectives.

➢ VERY:- It can be used to qualify both positive

and negative adjectives

Application to the Given Question

"...the liquid was very hot to drink comfortably without causing a severe burn..."

Because the sentence describes a situation where drinking the soup would cause a "severe burn" (a negative consequence/inability), the adverb "very" is insufficient. We need "too" to link the extreme heat to the inability to drink it safely.

Corrected Sentence Even though the waiter had warned us that the soup had just been removed from the stove, the liquid was too hot to drink comfortably without causing a severe burn to the tongue.

More Examples for Clarity

  • He is very old. (Neutral statement of age) ✅

  • He is too old to run a marathon. (Negative result: He cannot run) ✅

  • The box is very heavy. (It’s heavy, but I might still lift it) ✅

  • The box is too heavy to lift. (Negative result: I cannot lift it) ✅
